title: The Model Hears You: Audio Language Model Deployments Should Consider the Principle of Least Privilege
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not conduct benchmarks specifically measuring faith or religion. It mentions religion as a protected characteristic under civil rights law in the context of potential model discrimination based on voice features.
findings: The paper does not present any specific findings related to religion. It highlights that audio language models could potentially discriminate based on protected attributes, which legally include religion, but does not test this hypothesis empirically. The core findings are about risks of identity inference, gender bias, and emotion detection from audio.
